symptom: A user task created with `targeting groups xpath [Name = 'Reviewers']` was stored correctly (`UserTargeting: Workflows$XPathGroupTargeting`), but `describe workflow` printed it with no targeting clause, so describe -> create or modify silently removed the targeting. Users xpath, users microflow and groups microflow on the same workflow described fine
cause: userSourceFromGen, the reader's switch from the polymorphic UserSource/UserTargeting part to sdk/workflows, had a case for every targeting $Type the writer emits except Workflows$XPathGroupTargeting, which fell through to NoUserSource. The writer (userTargetingToGen) and the describe formatter (the XPathGroupSource case in cmd_workflows.go) both handled it, so reading the formatter and the writer showed nothing wrong
insight: When a describe clause is missing but the formatter has a case for it, the reader is the suspect: a missing case in a type switch on decoded gen types defaults silently. A table test that round-trips EVERY value the writer can emit through encode -> decode -> read catches the whole class, not just the reported kind; the per-kind tests that existed covered only the kinds someone had happened to describe. The executor's `TestRoundtripWorkflow_XPathTargeting` (integration) replays the describe output and compares, with the users-xpath task as the control
fix: Add the `*genWf.XPathGroupTargeting` -> `&workflows.XPathGroupSource{XPath: s.XPathConstraint()}` case; table test over all five targeting kinds, single and multi user task
